headline: Taiwan's China Airlines and EVA Air continue flying over Russia on Europe routes'
dek: As of Tuesday Nov 3, flight trackers showed Taiwan's two carriers — China Airlines and EVA Air — continuing to cross Russian airspace on flights between Taipei and Frankfurt, Munich, Paris and Vienna, after having voluntarily avoided Russian airspace since Feb 2022. Trigger: Pakistan briefly…
sources: Nikkei Asia, citing flight trackers and Taiwan's transport minister's Oct 28 remarks
fault_line: Sanctions fairness or survival routing? Should Taiwan's carriers keep the Russia shortcut while European rivals are locked out of it — or is this just what a one-day Pakistan ban forced?

sections.what_happened: As of Tuesday Nov 3, flight trackers showed Taiwan's two carriers — China Airlines and EVA Air — continuing to cross Russian airspace on flights between Taipei and Frankfurt, Munich, Paris and Vienna, after having voluntarily avoided Russian airspace since Feb 2022. Trigger: Pakistan briefly revoked overflight rights for Taiwanese airlines on Oct 28 (reportedly citing Beijing's 'One China' position), forcing a reroute over the Baltic Sea, Finland, Russia and Japan; Taiwan's transport minister said Oct 28 airlines may choose routes that best suit operations, which the carriers appear to have taken as a green light. Both airlines declined to comment to Nikkei. European carriers have suspended or reduced China service since 2022 because they cannot compete with carriers that can fly over Russia.
sections.what_verified: Nikkei Asia only (T2); flight-tracker data cited within the same report does not add a publisher family
sections.what_disputed: No European-government or EU statement in the report beyond 'rattled Europeans' framing; the carriers' own rationale is unstated (declined comment) — the 'green light' reading of the minister's remark is Nikkei's inference, not a carrier statement.
sections.why_matters: Not a proven-set story (demand capped); monitor for a European-government reaction or a Pakistan/Beijing statement that would lift it. No Short on the routing fact alone.
